title: Jacobi-Zariski exact sequence for H_1 of naive cotangent complexes (Stacks 00S2)
statement:
Let $A\to B\xrightarrow{\ \varphi\ }C$ be homomorphisms of commutative rings, $C$ an $A$-algebra through the composite. For a ring map $R\to S$ let $\mathrm{NL}_{S/R}=\bigl(I_{S/R}/I_{S/R}^2\xrightarrow{\delta_{S/R}}\bigoplus_{s\in S}S\,\mathrm d[s]\bigr)$ be the naive cotangent complex of [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map], formed with the canonical presentation $R[S]\to S$, $[s]\mapsto s$, with kernel $I_{S/R}$, and $H_1(L_{S/R})=\ker\delta_{S/R}$; $\Omega$ and $\mathrm d$ are as in [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. Let $\mathrm{NL}_{B/A}\otimes_BC$ be the complex $I_{B/A}/I_{B/A}^2\otimes_BC\xrightarrow{\delta_{B/A}\otimes\mathrm{id}_C}\bigoplus_{b\in B}C\,\mathrm d[b]$ and $H_1(\mathrm{NL}_{B/A}\otimes_BC)$ its kernel. Define $C$-linear maps:
(a) $u:H_1(\mathrm{NL}_{B/A}\otimes_BC)\to H_1(L_{C/A})$, the restriction of $I_{B/A}/I_{B/A}^2\otimes_BC\to I_{C/A}/I_{C/A}^2$, $(g\bmod I_{B/A}^2)\otimes c\mapsto c\cdot(\varphi_\sharp(g)\bmod I_{C/A}^2)$, where $\varphi_\sharp:A[B]\to A[C]$ is the $A$-algebra map $[b]\mapsto[\varphi(b)]$ (the functoriality of $\mathrm{NL}$ for the square $A=A$, $\varphi:B\to C$);
(b) $v:H_1(L_{C/A})\to H_1(L_{C/B})$, the restriction of $I_{C/A}/I_{C/A}^2\to I_{C/B}/I_{C/B}^2$ induced by the ring map $A[C]\to B[C]$ that is $A\to B$ on coefficients and $[c]\mapsto[c]$ (the functoriality of $\mathrm{NL}$ for the square $A\to B$, $C=C$);
(c) $w:C\otimes_B\Omega_{B/A}\to\Omega_{C/A}$, $c\otimes\mathrm db\mapsto c\,\mathrm d\varphi(b)$, and $z:\Omega_{C/A}\to\Omega_{C/B}$, $c\,\mathrm dc'\mapsto c\,\mathrm dc'$.
Then $u$ and $v$ are well defined (they land in the kernels), and there is a $C$-linear map $\partial:H_1(L_{C/B})\to C\otimes_B\Omega_{B/A}$ (the connecting map of the snake lemma; explicitly, if $h=g\bmod I_{C/B}^2\in H_1(L_{C/B})$ with $g=\sum_\alpha b_\alpha[c]^\alpha\in I_{C/B}$ written in the monomials $[c]^\alpha$ of $B[C]$ with coefficients $b_\alpha\in B$, then $\partial(h)=\sum_\alpha\gamma_{C/B}([c]^\alpha)\otimes\mathrm db_\alpha$, where $\gamma_{C/B}:B[C]\to C$ is the canonical presentation) such that the sequence of $C$-modules
$$H_1(\mathrm{NL}_{B/A}\otimes_BC)\xrightarrow{u}H_1(L_{C/A})\xrightarrow{v}H_1(L_{C/B})\xrightarrow{\partial}C\otimes_B\Omega_{B/A}\xrightarrow{w}\Omega_{C/A}\xrightarrow{z}\Omega_{C/B}\to0$$
is exact. Moreover, if $\operatorname{Tor}^B_1(\Omega_{B/A},C)=0$ and $\operatorname{Tor}^B_2(\Omega_{B/A},C)=0$ [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules], then the natural $C$-linear map $H_1(L_{B/A})\otimes_BC\to H_1(\mathrm{NL}_{B/A}\otimes_BC)$, $h\otimes c\mapsto h\otimes c$, is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Construct u by restricting the lifted conormal map of the canonical presentation to the base-changed kernel. Commutation with cotangentComplex shows it lands in H1(L_C/A). Construct t as LinearMap.tensorKer C C applied to the canonical presentation differential. Its pure-tensor formula and the ambient formula for u are definitional equalities. These are real constructions, with no chosen unproved data.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00S2 (lemma-exact-sequence-NL), lines 35411--35485 (tag verified in stacks-project/tags/tags: 00S2,algebra-lemma-exact-sequence-NL)

proof.text: For exactness at H1(L_C/A), use the composite presentation F = Q.comp P and its presentation equivalence e with the canonical presentation E. Mathlib Generators.Cotangent.exact gives a preimage x of each cycle e(y) annihilated by the map to Q. Generators.H1Cotangent.map_comp_cotangentComplex_baseChange and Generators.CotangentSpace.map_toComp_injective imply x is in the base-changed kernel. Extension.Cotangent.map_sub_map shows that any two presentation maps agree on this base-changed kernel: their difference factors through the base-changed differential. This identifies the preimage with u(x). Conversely, compose the two conormal maps and apply Generators.Cotangent.exact.apply_apply_eq_zero. The composite-presentation conormal exactness and differential injection are already proved in Mathlib.RingTheory.Kaehler.JacobiZariski; their polynomial-kernel and basis inputs are the cited leaves.

proof.text: Apply Mathlib Algebra.H1Cotangent.exact_map_δ and exact_δ_mapBaseChange for exactness at H1(L_C/B) and C tensor Omega_B/A. These are the already-proved presentation snake argument, with the cokernel identification obtained from the conormal exact sequence and tensor right exactness. Apply KaehlerDifferential.exact_mapBaseChange_map and map_surjective for the final exactness and surjectivity. Thus no diagram or connecting map needs to be chosen anew.

proof.text: For the coefficient formula, identify the given h with the subtype represented by Cotangent.mk g, using injectivity of its inclusion. Apply Mathlib Generators.H1Cotangent.δ_eq_δAux, write g as its finite monomial sum with MvPolynomial.as_sum, and apply δAux_monomial to each summand. The canonical Q has val = id, yielding precisely the stated product of powers.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00S2 (lemma-exact-sequence-NL), lines 35411--35485 (tag verified in stacks-project/tags/tags: 00S2,algebra-lemma-exact-sequence-NL)

proof.text: For the Tor criterion, apply the existing bijective_twoTermKernelBaseChange_algebra to the ULift of the presentation differential. Freeness is transported along the ring equivalence ULift B = B and the module equivalence for ULift. Exactness and surjectivity of toKaehler identify the lifted cokernel with ULift Omega_B/A by the first isomorphism theorem. Map this isomorphism through Tor to obtain its degree-one and degree-two vanishing hypotheses. Explicit kernel and tensor equivalences transport the resulting bijectivity back to tensorKer C C. The commuting square is checked on pure tensors and extended by tensor induction. This transport uses no Tor invariance theorem between different universes; every Tor in the application stays in the same lifted ModuleCat.

lean.statement: theorem jacobiZariski_homology_sequence (A : Type u) (B : Type v) (C : Type w) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [CommRing C] [Algebra A B] [Algebra B C] [Algebra A C] [IsScalarTower A B C] : let P := (Generators.self A B).toExtension let Q := (Generators.self B C).toExtension let E := (Generators.self A C).toExtension let K := (P.cotangentComplex.baseChange C).ker let f := Extension.Cotangent.map (Generators.defaultHom (Generators.self A B) (Generators.self A C)).toExtensionHom let v := H1Cotangent.map A B C C let w := KaehlerDifferential.mapBaseChange A B C let z := KaehlerDifferential.map A B C C let δ := H1Cotangent.δ A B C ∃ (u : K →ₗ[C] H1Cotangent A C) (t : C ⊗[B] H1Cotangent A B →ₗ[C] K), (∀ x : K, E.h1Cotangentι (u x) = f.liftBaseChange C x.val) ∧ (∀ (c : C) (h : H1Cotangent A B), (t (c ⊗ₜ[B] h)).val = c ⊗ₜ[B] P.h1Cotangentι h) ∧ (∀ (g : Q.ker) (h : H1Cotangent B C), Q.h1Cotangentι h = Extension.Cotangent.mk g → δ h = ∑ α ∈ g.val.support, (α.prod (fun c n ↦ c ^ n)) ⊗ₜ[B] D A B (MvPolynomial.coeff α g.val)) ∧ Function.Exact u v ∧ Function.Exact v δ ∧ Function.Exact δ w ∧ Function.Exact w z ∧ Function.Surjective z ∧ ((IsZero (((Tor' (ModuleCat (ULift.{max u v w} B)) 1).obj (ModuleCat.of (ULift.{max u v w} B) (ULift.{max u v w} Ω[B⁄A]))).obj (ModuleCat.of (ULift.{max u v w} B) (ULift.{max u v w} C))) ∧ IsZero (((Tor' (ModuleCat (ULift.{max u v w} B)) 2).obj (ModuleCat.of (ULift.{max u v w} B) (ULift.{max u v w} Ω[B⁄A]))).obj (ModuleCat.of (ULift.{max u v w} B) (ULift.{max u v w} C)))) → Function.Bijective t)
